zh.title: Honeywell 領導聯盟氫電推進突破 歐洲 18 公司完成系統整合
zh.summary: Honeywell 領導 18 歐洲公司完成氫電推進系統整合；下一階段將在義大利進行地面示範。
body: Honeywell Aerospace 領導的歐洲聯盟在 2026 年 9 月 17 日宣布，旗下 Project NEWBORN 成功將各子系統整合為一個功能性氫電力來源，能為飛機產生並供應電能。該聯盟由來自 10 國的 18 家公司、大學及研究機構組成，包含 PowerCell、Fraunhofer、Test-Fuchs、Siemens Industry Software、KU Leuven、Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg 及 CIRA。
測試平台設於布拉格附近研究中心，具備電源、流體分配、電力系統、控制室、安全設備及散熱系統。專案協調員 Miroslav Matoušek 指出，NEWBORN 不僅展示新技術，更證明歐洲產學研能合作實現雄心願景。
下一步將進行完整推進系統的整合地面示範：氫電力來源與電池將為驅動螺旋槳的電動馬達供電。氫燃料電池電源將轉移至義大利 Gorizia，最終測試將把數十項在歐洲各地開發的技術整合為單一功能單元。
燃料電池電源將連接 Pipistrel 的電池系統，以及由諾丁漢大學、Honeywell Aerospace 與 Pipistrel 聯合開發的百萬瓦級電動推進系統。技術負責人 Ondřej Kotaba 說，從空氣供應、氫氣管理、熱管理到電力分配、功率電子、控制、通訊與安全監控，所有子系統匯聚將是專案的高潮。
專案由歐盟透過 Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking 資助，目標是打造同類中全球最強大的氫電飛機推進系統之一。

en.title: Honeywell-Led Alliance Achieves Hydrogen-Electric Propulsion Breakthrough with 18 European Partners
en.summary: Honeywell-led consortium integrates hydrogen power source; ground demonstration planned in Italy next.
body: A Honeywell Aerospace-led alliance of 18 European companies announced on 17 September 2026 that Project NEWBORN has successfully integrated individual subsystems into a functional hydrogen power source capable of generating and supplying electrical energy for aircraft. The consortium comprises companies, universities and research organisations from 10 countries, including PowerCell, Fraunhofer, Test-Fuchs, Siemens Industry Software, KU Leuven, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and CIRA.

The test platform, based at a research centre near Prague, includes its own power source, working fluid distribution systems, electrical systems, a control room, safety equipment and heat rejection systems. Project Coordinator Miroslav Matoušek said NEWBORN demonstrates not only new technology but the ability of European industry, universities and research organisations to work together on ambitious technological visions and turn them into functioning systems.

The next step will be an integrated ground demonstration of the complete propulsion system, in which the hydrogen power source and batteries will supply electricity to an electric motor driving an aircraft propeller. The hydrogen power source system will be transferred to Gorizia, Italy, for the continuation of the project. Final tests in Gorizia will bring together dozens of technologies developed at different locations across Europe into a single functional unit.

The fuel-cell power source will be connected to battery systems from Pipistrel and a megawatt-class electric propulsion system jointly developed by the University of Nottingham, Honeywell Aerospace and Pipistrel. Technology Fellow Ondřej Kotaba noted that a range of interconnected technologies — from air supply and conditioning, hydrogen management and thermal management to electrical distribution, power electronics, control, communications and safety monitoring — have been developed in parallel, and bringing all subsystems together represents the culmination of the project.
Funded by the European Union through the EU Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking, NEWBORN aims to build one of the world's most powerful hydrogen-electric aircraft propulsion systems of its kind.
